stem: The student wants to describe the primary purpose of the Linden Telescope. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:

- The Harrow Telescope, built in 1998, has a 4.1-meter mirror and is used to study distant galaxies.
- The Linden Telescope, built in 2006, has a 2.3-meter mirror.
- The Linden Telescope is used mainly to track asteroids whose orbits bring them near Earth.
- The third telescope, the Oriel, is reserved for training graduate students.
choices: The Linden Telescope, which was built in 2006, has a mirror that measures 2.3 meters across.
The Linden Telescope at the Vela Ridge Observatory is used mainly to track near-Earth asteroids.
The Vela Ridge Observatory, home of the Linden Telescope, houses three telescopes in Chile.
Unlike the Linden Telescope, the Harrow Telescope is used to study galaxies that are very distant.
explanation: The goal names one telescope and one feature: the Linden Telescope's purpose. Choice B makes the Linden Telescope its subject and uses its main clause to state that purpose, tracking near-Earth asteroids.

A.why: You saw the right name and stopped checking. This choice describes the Linden Telescope's construction date and mirror size, not what the telescope is used for.

C.why: You picked a sentence about the whole observatory. The Linden Telescope appears only in a side clause, and the sentence says nothing about its purpose.

D.why: The purpose in this sentence belongs to the Harrow Telescope. The Linden Telescope is mentioned only as a point of contrast, and its own purpose is never given.

stem: The student wants to describe the process by which Calcara repairs cracks. Which choice does NOT effectively use relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices: In Calcara, water entering a crack activates dormant bacterial spores, and the bacteria then produce limestone that gradually fills the gap.

Choice C mentions the office and the year 1915, but the accomplishment it describes, leading the highlands mapping, happened after she joined. It's from the wrong period. Choice A describes the 1908 delta map, B the 1912 atlas, and D both of those, and all of them come before 1915.

A.why: This choice ends by mentioning the National Survey Office, and you may have taken that as a sign it was about her time there. The office is only a reference point. The accomplishment itself, the 1908 delta map, comes before she joined.

B.why: You may have doubted the 'three years before' figure because no note states it. It follows from the dates: the atlas came in 1912 and she joined in 1915. The sentence is accurate and describes a pre-office accomplishment.

D.why: You may have rejected this choice because it combines two accomplishments when the goal says 'an accomplishment.' Both took place before 1915, so the sentence still describes what she achieved before joining the office.

stem: The student wants to specify how much longer the comet's orbit has taken since its 2011 encounter with Jupiter. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Halvorsen-3 is a short-period comet first observed in 1987.
• Its icy nucleus measures about 3 kilometers across.
• Before 2011, the comet took 6.2 years to complete one orbit around the Sun.
• In 2011, the comet passed unusually close to Jupiter.
• Jupiter's gravity stretched the comet's path, and Halvorsen-3 now takes 7.9 years to orbit the Sun.
choices: Halvorsen-3, a short-period comet with a nucleus about 3 kilometers across, was first observed in 1987 and passed close to Jupiter in 2011.
Since passing close to Jupiter in 2011, Halvorsen-3 has taken 7.9 years to orbit the Sun, 1.7 years longer than its earlier 6.2-year orbit.
Since passing close to Jupiter in 2011, Halvorsen-3 has needed a full 7.9 years to complete each of its orbits around the distant Sun.
When Halvorsen-3 passed close to Jupiter in 2011, the giant planet's gravity stretched the comet's path and lengthened its orbit around the Sun.
explanation: The goal asks for one specific detail: HOW MUCH LONGER the orbit has become since 2011. That is a gap between two numbers, so you need both the old period (6.2 years) and the new one (7.9 years), or the difference between them. Choice B gives the new period and says outright that it is 1.7 years longer than the old one, so it does exactly what the goal asks.

A.why: You picked a sentence that names the right comet and the 2011 encounter, but it tells you about the comet's size and when it was discovered. It says nothing about how long its orbit takes.

C.why: This is the subtype's trap. It gives you the new orbital period, but only one of the two numbers. 'How much longer' asks for the difference, and nothing here compares 7.9 years with the old 6.2-year period.

D.why: You chose the sentence that explains why the orbit changed. It tells you the orbit got longer but never says by how much, and the amount is the detail the goal names.

stem: The student wants to describe the method Reiner used in his study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Cleaner wrasses are small reef fish that eat parasites off larger "client" fish.
• Marine biologist Tomasz Reiner asked whether wrasses treat clients more honestly when other fish are watching.
• He set up tanks where a wrasse fed from a plate, half with a bystander fish visible behind glass and half with an empty compartment.
• Watched wrasses took the forbidden food 40% less often than unwatched ones.
• Reiner concluded that wrasses protect their reputations.
choices: Marine biologist Tomasz Reiner set out to learn whether cleaner wrasses, which eat parasites off larger fish, behave more honestly when watched.
Reiner had cleaner wrasses feed from plates in tanks, half with a bystander fish visible behind glass and half with an empty compartment.
In Reiner's study, cleaner wrasses with a bystander fish watching took the forbidden food 40% less often than wrasses that were not watched.
From his work with cleaner wrasses, Reiner concluded that these small reef fish act to protect their reputations among the other fish.
explanation: The notes follow the order of a study: background, the question, the method, the result, and the conclusion. The goal asks for one stage only, the METHOD, meaning what Reiner actually did. Choice B describes his setup: wrasses feeding from plates, with a bystander fish visible in half the tanks and an empty compartment in the other half. Reiner and his setup are the main subject of the sentence.

A.why: This is the subtype's trap. It names Reiner and his study, but it gives the question he wanted to answer, not how he went about answering it. You matched the name instead of the stage the goal asks for.

C.why: You picked the study's result. The 40% gap between watched and unwatched wrasses is what Reiner found, not how he found it.

D.why: This gives Reiner's conclusion, which is the last stage of the study. It tells you nothing about the tanks or the procedure.

stem: The student wants to state how much the rural vaccination rate changed during the program's first year. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 2021, Corvale County began sending mobile flu-vaccine clinics to its rural towns.
• In 2020, before the program, 31% of the county's rural adults got a flu vaccine.
• In 2021, the program's first year, that rate rose to 44%.
• In 2023, the clinics added evening hours, and the rural rate reached 52%.
• The county's urban vaccination rate stayed near 50% throughout this period.
choices: By 2023, after Corvale County's clinics added evening hours, the rural flu vaccination rate had climbed 21 percentage points above its 2020 level.
In 2021, Corvale County's mobile clinics raised the rural flu vaccination rate to 44%, bringing it closer to the county's urban rate of about 50%.
In 2021, the first year of Corvale County's mobile clinics, the rural flu vaccination rate rose 13 percentage points, from 31% to 44%.
Corvale County began sending mobile flu-vaccine clinics to its rural towns in 2021 and then extended their schedules with evening hours in 2023.
explanation: Underline the restriction in the goal: the change in the rural rate during the program's FIRST YEAR. That means 2020 compared with 2021. Choice C picks out that year and gives the gap directly: up 13 percentage points, from 31% to 44%.

A.why: This is the subtype's trap. It describes a real change in the rural rate, but over the wrong period. The 21-point rise runs through 2023, after evening hours were added, not just the first year.

B.why: You chose a sentence that compares the rural rate with the urban rate. The goal asks how much the rural rate changed from its own starting point, and this choice never gives the 2020 figure.

D.why: This sentence describes how the program grew over time, but it gives no vaccination rates, so it can't tell you how much anything changed.
